threads.thread_goal: Align on overall program scope, objectives, and roles for the pilot.

messages.text: Hello team, welcome to the official channel for our Integrated Creative Wellbeing Program pilot! The goal is to design and test a multidisciplinary program for our residents. Let's start by confirming the high-level scope.
Based on the project brief, we are planning for an 8-week pilot. Can we all agree on this duration as our primary timeframe? This will help us structure the curriculum in A1.

Thanks for kicking this off. The 8-week duration sounds perfect. It gives us enough time to see engagement patterns. I've already started outlining the movement session plan for T2 and this timeframe works well.

Good morning. An 8-week pilot is a solid plan. I'm happy to support. For my role, I'll be reviewing session plans like T1 and T2 to ensure they are culturally and spiritually sensitive for all residents.
Agreed on 8 weeks. My focus will be on ensuring all activities have clear safety protocols. I'll need to work closely with you @97658 and @23126 on the practical side of your sessions.
Ok, 8 weeks is fine. I will need to know what rooms you need soon.
Absolutely, @266482. That's covered under T4, and we'll tackle the detailed schedule in our next thread. For now, let's focus on roles.
Hi everyone. Sorry for the delay. 8 weeks sounds good. Where should I put the music session templates when they are ready?
No problem, @23126. All session templates, including yours for T1, will be consolidated in the Program Curriculum document, which is A1. I've just created the file and will share the link shortly.

Great, we have consensus on D1. Now for roles (D2). To summarize:
- I'll handle overall program structure (T3) and resident comms.
- @97658 and @23126 will design the core dance (T2) and music (T1) sessions.
- @266482 will manage room/resource mapping (T4) and facility constraints.
- @362587 will provide spiritual/cultural review and define eligibility.
- @455451 will own all safety and emergency procedures.
Does this accurately capture our primary responsibilities?
Looks correct to me. Clear and concise.
Yes, that covers my area. Thanks.
That aligns with my understanding. Thank you.
yes that's fine
Ok I understand.
Excellent. We've confirmed the pilot duration (D1) and our core roles (D2). We have a solid foundation to build on.

Next steps: I will start drafting the overall schedule (T3). @97658 and @23126, please continue with your session plans for T2 and T1. I'll start a new thread for the schedule review tomorrow morning.
Sounds good. I'll have a draft of T2 ready for review by then.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize weekly schedule, room allocation, and staffing feasibility.

messages.text: Morning all. As promised, here is the first draft of the weekly schedule for the pilot. Please see the 'Schedule' tab in A2. I've tried to balance session types and avoid major facility events. Feedback is welcome, especially from @266482 on room availability (T4) and @455451 on staffing impact (T9).
Thanks. I looked at it. Tuesday morning at 10am in the main hall won't work, that's when the floors are deep cleaned. We can't move that.

Good catch, @266482. I also noticed the Tuesday slot was for my movement session. The main hall is ideal, but the Community Room could work as an alternative. Could we swap it to Tuesday afternoon at 2pm? That seems to be free in A2.

Looking at the schedule, the mixed-ability movement session will require at least two staff members present for safety and assistance, in addition to the therapist. We need to ensure that's factored into the staffing model (T9). The other sessions seem manageable with one staff member supporting.
Excellent suggestions. @266482, would the Community Room at 2pm on Tuesdays work for you? I've updated A2 with that proposed change.

Thanks, @455451. That's a critical point. Let's formalize that: for all movement sessions, we will have 1 therapist + 2 support staff. For all other sessions, 1 therapist + 1 support staff. This will be our confirmed staffing model. Does anyone see an issue with this?
Yes, Tuesday 2pm in the Community Room is fine. The staffing model also seems ok, I don't think it will cause overtime issues.

The staffing model is good. I can build the staff briefing for T11 around this. It also means the pre-session safety checklist (A5) needs to be signed by one of the support staff, not just the therapist.
The schedule looks fine from my perspective. No clashes with any planned prayer times or spiritual gatherings. Thank you for checking.
The quiet room is listed for my music session. How many people can it hold?
Hi @23126, the capacity for each room is listed in the 'Rooms' tab of A2. The quiet room is listed with a capacity of 6.
Perfect. With the Tuesday session moved and confirmed, and no other objections, I think we can approve the weekly schedule and room plan as updated in A2.
To summarize, we've approved the final schedule (D3) and the staffing model (D4). This is a huge step forward. Thanks everyone for the quick and effective feedback.
Next step: @455451, you can now proceed with drafting the safety procedures (T6) and the staff briefing (T11) based on this confirmed plan.
Will do. I'll post a draft of the safety protocols for review by end of day tomorrow.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on safety, emergency, and incident reporting procedures.

messages.text: Hi team, as per my action from the last thread, I've drafted the safety protocols. Please review the document A3. It covers the pre-session checklist (A5), emergency escalation, and incident reporting, fulfilling T6. I'd appreciate your feedback.

Thanks @455451. This is very thorough. For the pre-session checklist A5, could we add a specific item to check for 'clear, dry, and unobstructed floor space'? It's critical for the movement sessions to prevent slips and falls.
The document mentions first aid kits. Who is responsible for making sure they are stocked?

This looks very comprehensive. A question on the incident report template: would it be possible to add an optional field to note if spiritual care was offered or requested by the resident? It can be an important part of responding to distress.
What if a resident starts crying during a music session because a song brings up a memory? Do I need to fill out an incident report for that?

That's a great question, @23126. Generally, an emotional response that you can manage therapeutically within the session is part of the process, not an incident. The protocol in A3 defines an incident as something that requires intervention beyond the session's scope, like a medical issue or a resident becoming a danger to themselves or others. @455451 does that sound right?
Yes, @71781 has it exactly right. An incident is when the situation escalates beyond the planned activity. Thanks for the clarification.
The version with the spiritual care field is more holistic. My vote is for that one.
I agree, let's go with the template that includes the spiritual care note. It's better to have the option. Let's consider that our selected incident reporting template.

Okay, decision made. I'll remove the other version and finalize A3 with the chosen template. With the checklist updated and the template selected, are we all comfortable signing off on the safety checklist and emergency escalation steps as documented?
Yes, they look solid. I approve.
Approved from my side.
looks ok to me
Great. We've now signed off on the safety checklist and escalation steps (D5) and selected the incident report template (D6). I'll use this finalized content for the staff briefing materials (T11).

threads.thread_goal: Define resident eligibility, consent, and communication approach.

messages.text: Good morning team. I've drafted the resident eligibility and referral criteria for the pilot, as per T10. The goal is to be inclusive while ensuring the program is suitable for the residents' wellbeing needs. I've also cross-referenced our Spiritual and Cultural Sensitivity Guide (A4). Please take a look and share your thoughts.

Thanks @362587! Building on that, here is the draft Resident Information and Consent Pack (A6), which covers T7. It's written in plain language to be as clear as possible. @97658 and @23126, could you please review both documents from a therapeutic standpoint?

These look great. One small suggestion for the eligibility criteria in T10: the section on physical ability could be phrased more positively. Instead of listing what people *can't* do, maybe we can say 'sessions can be adapted for various mobility levels, including seated participation'. It might feel more welcoming.
Do we need to get them to sign the consent form before every session?

I've reviewed A6. It's clear that participation is voluntary, which is good. Does it also state that choosing not to participate will have no impact on their standard care or accommodation status? That needs to be explicit.
Hi @23126, the consent form in A6 covers participation in the entire 8-week pilot program, so it only needs to be signed once at the beginning.
Good point, @455451. That is a critical detail. I've added a sentence to A6 to make that explicitly clear. Thank you.
I really like that suggestion, @97658. It's much more inclusive. I'll update the wording in T10 right away. With that change, are we happy to approve the eligibility and referral criteria?
Yes, with that change, it has my approval.
Looks good to me too. Let's consider D7 approved.
How are we giving these forms to residents and getting them back?

Good logistical question, @266482. I propose that frontline care staff distribute the info packs (A6) during their regular interactions. Residents can then return the signed forms to the front desk, where we can have a dedicated collection box. Does that process work for your team?
yes that is fine.
Great. With the final wording tweaks and a clear distribution plan, are we ready to approve the resident information and consent materials in A6?
Approved.
Approved.

Excellent. D7 and D8 are now locked in. We have a clear and respectful process for inviting residents to the program. My next step for T7 is to get the final A6 materials printed and ready for distribution.

threads.thread_goal: Align on tracking, evaluation, and reporting for the pilot outcomes.

messages.text: Hi team, let's align on how we'll track engagement and evaluate the pilot's success. This covers T8 and T12. @23126, as the owner of T8, could you share your initial thoughts on a simple wellbeing tracking method?
I was thinking we could use a standardized clinical depression scale before and after the 8 weeks. Or I could write detailed session notes on each resident and we could analyze them.

A full clinical scale might be too intensive for this pilot and could feel intimidating for residents. For T8, we need something lightweight that staff can administer quickly and consistently. What about a simple pre- and post-session mood check? We could use a 1-5 scale or even a visual scale with smiley faces.
I support the simple approach. It's less prone to error and protects resident confidentiality better than detailed notes. We can log the data easily in the A7 tracking sheet.
The visual scale with faces is an excellent idea. It transcends language and literacy, making it very accessible.
The consensus is clear. Let's go with a simple pre/post session mood check (visual scale) plus attendance tracking. This will be our minimal data set for collection. That settles D9.

Now for the evaluation. For my task T12, I'll need to create the Pilot Evaluation Summary Report (A8). I propose a concise 2-page report for facility management. It would include attendance stats, a summary of the mood data from A7, and key qualitative themes from staff/resident feedback. Does this format and audience sound right?
Yes, management will want a short summary. That works.
Agreed. The report should definitely end with clear recommendations on what to keep, change, or expand if the program continues.
Perfect. So we're agreed on the format and audience for the final report: a 2-page summary for management, including data, themes, and recommendations. That confirms D10.
So for T8 I just need to use the smiley face chart and record attendance?

Exactly, @23126. All session leaders will do the same. I will set up the columns in the A7 tracking log for everyone to use consistently. Your task for T8 will be to formally document this simple procedure so we can train staff on it.
Great discussion. We've confirmed our data collection method (D9) and the final report format (D10). We're all set for the evaluation phase.
